what_it_does: Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) is a statistical technique used to answer 'what if' questions in causal reasoning and probabilistic modeling — it works by generating thousands of random samples from a probability distribution and checking whether each sample matches the data well enough to keep. This is inherently sequential: you can't start generating the next sample until you know whether to accept or reject the current one. PROCA is a programmable hardware accelerator that speeds this up in two ways. First, it uses processing-in-memory units — computing circuits embedded directly inside RAM chips so data doesn't have to travel far — to generate samples faster. Second, it predicts whether a sample will be accepted before the full check is complete, so it can get a head start computing the next sample in parallel, like a chef prepping the next dish before the previous one is served.
